=== L270
**EM-26 — Dirty keys, the Lighting contract and the budget agreement.** Dirty keys are emitted for **emitters**, never for individual subjects (publish rule): a key `E/<emitter id>` — an int `(KIND << 32) | id` as in Graph LS-20 — fires on create, remove, `switch_on` flip, `shape_id` change, an `output_pm` change that crosses a bucket (`OUTPUT_DIRTY_QUANTUM_PM`, placeholder 50) and an integer `reach_px` step; continuous pose (origin, aim) never dirties — Lighting polls the read view at render rate, and keys wake only discrete presentation (a light switching on or off, a record spawning). Subject `lux` and `lit` are poll reads: sim consumers read inside their hook, presentation prompts poll at render rate, so a sweeping beam over 192 subjects cannot collapse notifications to `ALL` against `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256 (worst case here is every emitter, at most `MAX_EMITTERS` 96, in one tick). **The Lighting contract** (2D Lighting & Occlusion reads and never writes): per emitter `{id, kind, subkind, shape_id, origin_px, aim_units, half_angle_units, reach_px, r_lit_px, curve_class, output_pm, hue_class, lit, section_id, body_id, priority}` plus the shape table (`r_lit_px` is the sixteenth field, added by the 2026-10-27 design review; 2D Lighting's "15-field" wording is refreshed, Cross-References). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **The foot spill is published by a separate accessor** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the 16-field record describes a stored emitter and cannot represent the spill (a sub-contribution of the BEAM record centred on the foot, EM-6). `beam_spill(beam_id)` returns, while the beam is on and `BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX` > 0, the derived record `{beam_id, shape_id 11, origin_px (the foot origin `occ_origin`), reach_px (BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX), r_lit_px (the D.7 chain), curve_class SOFT, output_pm (BEAM_SPILL_PM), hue_class (the beam's), section_id, body_id, priority}` and null otherwise; it is not a record, has no id of its own and is **not in `emitters()`** (so `section_emission`, Attention's list and the 96-record cap never see it), and its changes dirty the beam's own key `E/<beam id>`. Lighting draws the pool from it and the build lint of AC-56 checks the drawn edge against `r_lit_px` ± 1 px, which is what lets "what you see lit is what the sim calls lit" be tested for the spill (AC-46c). This block publishes facts; Lighting conforms to them. Lighting owns textures, ambient, the canvas modulate, shadow-slot assignment (the sixth slot), the flash clamp (`flash_count` ≤ 3 per rolling second per light), flicker, gutter and decoy visuals; flicker is invisible to the query, which uses the steady mean. **Budget agreement (R17):** the sim never culls by view (an off-screen emitter still exposes — correct for P3); instead authoring lint keeps in-view emitter counts under Lighting's hypotheses (shadow-casting ≤ 6, non-shadow ≤ 24, node lanterns ≤ 8; art bible 8.10 budget shape and 8.11 flags 2 and 8), a debug assertion reports overflow, and every record carries a deterministic `priority` (default by kind: BEAM 255, BEACON 200, FIXTURE 120, DEPLOYABLE 100, FAULT_GLOW 80, NODE_LANTERN 60 — placeholder, owner technical-artist, confirmed by the Lighting spike) so Lighting's "emitters are cut before occlusion" is reproducible; a sim-lit but unrendered light would be a P1 lie, and the residual risk stays in Open Questions. A build lint asserts the rendered reach of every hard-edged row equals the table reach ±1 px.
=== L944
**What Lighting reads, and must not do.** Lighting reads the per-emitter read view (`id, kind, subkind, shape_id, origin_px, aim_units, half_angle_units, reach_px, r_lit_px, curve_class, output_pm, hue_class, lit, section_id, body_id, priority`, AC-46b) and `shapes()`, and it conforms to them: a texture's reach equals `reach_px` ± 1 px for every hard-edged row; a soft pool's readable boundary is drawn at the published actionable radius `r_lit_px` (D.7, an exact sim value) ± 1 px, so that a prompt appears exactly where the pool visibly ends (the sim/render agreement, AC-55 and AC-56, the load-bearing P1 test of the lighting stack); a dimmed emitter is drawn dimmer in proportion to `output_pm` (a lamp never renders brighter than the power it is served, Graph D.6). Lighting **owns** the light textures, ambient and `CanvasModulate`, shadow-slot assignment (lint hypotheses: at most 6 shadow-casting, 24 non-shadow and 8 node lanterns in view, art bible 8.10 and 8.11 flags 2 and 8; "emitters are cut before occlusion"), flicker and gutter, the per-light flash clamp (`flash_count` ≤ 3 per rolling 1 s, pipeline PR-13), and the decoy visuals of the Perception Filter. Lighting **must not**: write an emitter or any block; tell the sim a light is "culled"; give a decoy, a false lamp state or a flicker any query effect (the query reads `output_pm`, not the picture; AC-5a); move the true edge of a real light (art bible Principle 1; the stage-2 "cone seems to reach further" symptom is a **decoy glow past the true edge** with a palette leak, never a wider revealing radius, Cross-References refresh to 4.4); or draw a shadow with no occluder from a horror (actors and horrors never occlude, art bible 3.2, EM-20 c). Occlusion shadows follow the same footprint rectangles the query uses (one source for collision, light and shadow), and the same cell convention: Lighting's occluder polygon for a stored rectangle `[x0, x1) × [y0, y1)` is the continuous rectangle covering exactly those pixel cells, and an integer position is the centre of its cell (EM-20 a), so a drawn shadow has no seam where the query has none *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the shadow origin versus the sim's foot segment (EM-6, CP-5) is Open Question 5.

The tool-grip anchor `HAND_POINT` is lightless and is never read by this block, and no rule anywhere names it an origin. The beam follows *aim*, not facing: facing diverges from aim while running (PC-4 rule 3). The drawn cone and the simulated cone may diverge by up to the PC-5 accepted tolerance (≤ 2.8°, ≤ 1 tick; the Controller's `AIM_SEND_THRESHOLD` / `AIM_SETTLE_TICKS` knobs widen it to 3 ticks), which is why the agreement test (design test 1) is stated at rest. **Occlusion starts at the foot, not the chest** *(orchestrator ruling: the foot-origin rule of the technical-director over the systems-designer's sanitised walk-back, because `pos_curr` is outside every footprint by construction — `LocomotionStep` keeps the avatar's box out of them — and is free of the 2 px mirror jitter; the walk-back remains the documented alternative, ADR candidate 5)*: `CHEST_POINT.y` is -45..-25 px (`h` = −y, 25..45), so with a 24 px wall footprint the chest point stands *inside* the footprint whenever the feet are `s` px south of the first legal row in front of a north wall (`s` = 0 on that row, LY-8 b) with `h − 24 ≤ s ≤ h − 1`: the band is **1–44 px** over all animation rows (10–33 px for the walk row at `h` 34 — the first draft's "10-34" was one row's band, not the range). Walls east or west of the avatar cost at most the 4 px of chest-x offset. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The cone's apex, reach and distance are therefore measured from the chest, while the occluder segment to a subject starts at the foot origin (`pos_curr`, `beam_pose`). Other emitter kinds use their floor-plane anchor for both. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **What ships for each Lighting-spike outcome** (2D Lighting LO-10; its spike step 3b is a **pre-implementation gate for ADR candidate 5**, not a later check): outcome **B** (the light's `offset` moves the apex without moving the shadow origin) — the foot-origin rule ships as written and Lighting draws the shadow from the foot; outcome **A** (the shadow originates at the chest) with AC-57 passing — the foot-origin rule ships and the residual discrepancy (≤ 2 base px) is recorded; outcome A with AC-57 failing (a beam that renders black, or leaks through the wall, while the sim reports the opposite) — outcome **D** ships: ADR 5 adopts the walk-back (the sim occludes from the chest, walked back to the first clear point on the segment to the foot), D.4, EM-20 g and AC-10 are re-derived, and nothing else in this GDD changes. Until the spike reports, the foot-origin rule is the working rule and the worst case — a beam that renders black while the sim reports it lit, which would happen every time a player walks up to a wall — is an open risk (Open Question 5). **Near-field is aim-dependent, and the ruled answer is a drawn foot pool, not a control tax** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; ruled 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D24)*: an object between the lamp and the feet in screen-y is behind the apex when the player faces up-screen; the cone is honest about it (nothing in the drawn cone reaches it either) and the sim adds no hidden compensation.
